fieldValues.title: A decision is recorded as a hypothesis in its boundary
fieldValues.move: Every decision is written as an experiment, not a certainty. It names the boundary where it removes future options (the domain it is in-domain to: a choice that changes nothing at one level belongs to a tighter domain, and an ADR significant in code may be invisible at product level). It states the answer chosen as good enough for now (decision_statement) and why (rationale). It says what would make us reconsider (revisit_when), and what understeer and oversteer look like: the shadows of the poles it leans toward. A session comes back to it when a signal appears, when it does not achieve its goal, or when it stops working.
fieldValues.does_not_fix: Checking the signals: revisit_when is displayed but never checked today (handbook, Measurement and retrospective). Naming the decision's kind (the decision-taxonomy exercise). How a boundary is drawn: muDemocracy has laid out the decision record but not yet its boundary rules, and the boundary is still being learnt in this practice (owner, 2026-10-25); until then a decision names its domain as best it can, and the naming is itself part of the experiment.
fieldValues.falsifier: Decisions recorded this way are still not revisited when their signal appears, or still cannot say which boundary they hold in.
